narration.full_text: Welcome back, students! It's time for another quick quiz to test your understanding of control and coordination. Let's dive right in with our first question. What are the three main functions of the nervous system? Think about how it interacts with our environment and body. Take a moment to recall the key roles of this vital system. The three main functions are: collecting information from surroundings, controlling and coordinating muscle movement, and helping to recognize smell, taste, vision, and hearing with sense organs. Next question! Part A asks you to draw the structure of a neuron and label the cell body and axon. Part B asks: Name the part of the neuron where information is acquired, and through which information travels as an electrical impulse. For part B, information is acquired at the dendrite tip and travels as an electrical impulse from the dendrite to the cell body, then along the axon to its end. Moving on! Brain and spinal cord are two vital organs of our body. How is our body designed to protect them? Consider the structures that safeguard these delicate organs. Our body protects the brain inside a bony box called the cranium, with cerebrospinal fluid acting as a shock absorber. The spinal cord is protected by the vertebral column, or backbone. Here's our final question for this quiz. First, define a receptor and state its location in our body. Mention any two receptors present in our forebrain and their functions. Secondly, how do nerve impulses travel in our body? A receptor is a specialized tip of a nerve cell that receives information from the surroundings, located in sense organs. In the forebrain, gustatory receptors detect taste, and olfactory receptors detect smell. Nerve impulses travel as an electrical impulse created by a chemical reaction at the dendrite tip, moving to the cell body, along the axon, and then releasing chemicals across synapses. Great job, everyone! You've successfully navigated through some challenging questions about control and coordination. Keep up the excellent work!

visual_beats.description: Question: Write three main functions of the nervous system.

Answer:
(i) Collects information from the surroundings.
(ii) Controls and co-ordinates the movement of muscles.
(iii) Helps to recognise smell, taste, vision, hearing etc. with the help of sense organs.

Question:
(a) Draw the structure of neuron and label cell body and axon.
(b) Name the part of neuron:
(i) Where the information is acquired.
(ii) Through which information travels as an electrical impulse.

Answer (b):
(i) The information is acquired at the end of the dendrite tip of a nerve cell.
(ii) The information travels as an electrical impulse from the dendrite to the cell body and then along the axon to its end.
Question: 'Brain and Spinal cord are two vital organs of our body'. How is our body designed to protect them?

Answer: Brain is located inside a bony box, named as cranium and a fluid is present in this balloon, known as cerebrospinal fluid which is a shock absorber. Spinal cord is placed in a vertebral column and back bone protects it.

Question:
(i) Define receptor and state their location in our body. Mention any two receptors present in our forebrain and their functions.
(ii) How do nerve impulses travel in our body?

Answer (i):
Receptor: Specialised tips of some nerve cells which receive information from the surroundings.
Location: Sense organs
Gustatory receptor: Detect taste
Olfactory receptor: Detect smell

Answer (ii):
The information acquired at the end of the dendritic tip of a nerve cell, sets off a chemical reaction that creates an electrical impulse, which travels to the cell body, then along the axon to its end, releases some chemicals, across the synapses.
